title: The behavior of red foxes
body: Red foxes are solitary hunters that patrol their territory at dawn and dusk. They pounce on mice hidden under grass or snow, using their sharp hearing to pinpoint prey. In spring, pairs raise their kits in dens dug into banks, and their bushy tails help them balance and keep warm through the winter.

title: Vulpes vulpes: field notes on a widespread canid
body: Vulpes vulpes has the largest natural range of any wild carnivore, from Arctic tundra to city parks. Our field team logged individuals with russet coats, black legs and white-tipped tails resting in meadows and hunting voles at first light. Outside the breeding season V. vulpes lives mostly alone and is famous for its high-arcing mouse pounce.

title: How gray wolf packs hunt together
body: Gray wolves live and hunt in family packs led by a breeding pair. By coordinating long chases they can bring down elk and deer far larger than any single wolf. Howling keeps the pack together across miles of forest and warns rival packs away from their territory.

title: Canis lupus returns to Central Europe
body: After more than a century of absence, Canis lupus is recolonising the forests of Germany and western Poland. This grey-coated apex predator travels dozens of kilometres a night, and biologists track the new packs with camera traps and GPS collars. Farmers are relearning how to protect sheep with fences and shepherds.

title: Coyotes are moving into our cities
body: Coyotes have learned to thrive in North American cities, crossing parking lots at night and raising pups in overgrown lots. These adaptable wild canines eat rodents, fruit and whatever people leave out. Wildlife officials advise never feeding them so they keep their natural wariness of people.

title: Caring for a golden retriever
body: Golden retrievers are friendly, gentle family dogs with thick golden coats that need weekly brushing. They were bred to retrieve waterfowl, so they love to swim, fetch and carry things in their mouths. Plenty of exercise and early training keep this eager-to-please breed happy and calm.

title: How deer grow and shed their antlers
body: Every spring male deer begin growing a new set of antlers covered in soft velvet. By autumn the bone has hardened, the velvet is rubbed off on trees, and the stags use their antlers to spar during the rut. After the breeding season the antlers drop off and the cycle begins again.

title: What brown bears do all winter
body: Brown bears spend late summer and autumn eating huge amounts of berries, roots and salmon to build up fat. When snow arrives they retreat into a den and enter a deep winter sleep, living off their reserves for months. Mothers even give birth to cubs during this time.

title: The story of the Volkswagen Beetle
body: The Volkswagen Beetle, with its rounded body and rear-mounted air-cooled engine, became one of the best-selling cars ever built. Collectors still restore classic Beetles and show them off at vintage car meetings. Its simple mechanics made it easy to repair almost anywhere in the world.

title: Why commuting by bicycle beats driving
body: Riding a bicycle to work is cheap, healthy and often faster than sitting in city traffic. A simple bike with fenders, lights and a sturdy lock is all most commuters need. Many cities now have protected cycle lanes and secure bike parking near stations.

title: The secrets of a great Neapolitan pizza
body: A true Neapolitan pizza has a soft, blistered crust baked for about ninety seconds in a very hot wood-fired oven. The classic margherita keeps the toppings simple: San Marzano tomato, fresh mozzarella, basil and olive oil. The dough needs only flour, water, salt and yeast, but a long slow rise.

title: Making sushi rolls at home
body: Homemade sushi starts with properly seasoned short-grain rice and very fresh fish. Spread the rice on a sheet of nori, add salmon, avocado and cucumber, then roll it tightly with a bamboo mat. Slice the roll with a wet knife and serve with soy sauce, pickled ginger and wasabi.

title: What makes a truly great burger
body: A great hamburger starts with coarsely ground beef that is seasoned only with salt and cooked on a very hot grill. A toasted soft bun, melted cheese, crisp lettuce and ripe tomato finish it off. Resist pressing the patty flat, or the juices end up in the fire instead of the burger.

title: Building a better salad
body: A satisfying salad balances crisp leafy greens with colourful vegetables, something crunchy and a bright dressing. Toss tomatoes, peppers, cucumber and herbs with a simple lemon and olive oil vinaigrette. Add cheese, grains or grilled chicken to turn it into a full meal.

title: Riding the last steam railways
body: Heritage railways keep historic steam locomotives running, puffing clouds of white steam as they haul carriages through the countryside. Volunteers shovel coal into the firebox and keep the old engines in working order. For many visitors the whistle and smell of coal smoke are the highlight of the trip.

title: Planning your first motorcycle tour
body: A long-distance motorcycle trip needs a reliable bike, good riding gear and a realistic daily distance. Pack light in panniers, check tyre pressure and chain tension every morning, and plan fuel stops on quiet country roads. Riding with a helmet intercom makes group touring safer and more fun.

title: Winter hiking among snowy peaks
body: Hiking in snow-covered mountains rewards you with silent white slopes and sharp rocky summits under a clear sky. Winter routes demand crampons, warm layers and an eye on avalanche forecasts. Start early, because the short days leave little margin before dark.

title: Planning a tropical beach holiday
body: Picture white sand, palm trees leaning over turquoise water and nothing to do but swim and read in the shade. The best tropical beaches are quieter outside peak season. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and snorkelling gear to explore the calm lagoons.

title: Crossing the sand dunes of the Sahara
body: The Sahara's great sand seas are shaped by the wind into dunes that can rise hundreds of metres. Travellers cross them by camel or four-wheel drive, camping under enormous star-filled skies. At sunrise and sunset the ridges of golden sand glow orange and cast long shadows.

title: How to photograph waterfalls
body: To turn a rushing waterfall into silky white streams, use a tripod and a slow shutter speed of half a second or more. Overcast days avoid harsh highlights on the water and bring out the green moss on the rocks. A polarising filter cuts reflections from wet stones.

title: How to care for a pet parrot
body: Parrots are intelligent, long-lived birds that need a large cage, daily time outside it and plenty of toys to chew. A varied diet of pellets, fresh fruit and vegetables keeps their feathers bright. Many species can learn to talk and will bond closely with their owners.

title: Baking the perfect chocolate cake
body: A rich chocolate layer cake needs good cocoa, buttermilk and a little hot coffee to deepen the flavour. Bake the sponges until a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs, then cool them completely. Finish with a glossy chocolate ganache and fresh raspberries.

title: Learning to sail a small boat
body: A small sailing dinghy is the best way to learn how wind and sails work together. Beginners practise tacking and gybing on sheltered lakes before heading out to sea. Always wear a buoyancy aid and check the weather forecast before you launch.
